---
title = "Template Variants"
---

Template variants let you switch between alternative versions of any template on a per-document basis, without overriding the default.

## How it works

Add a `[tpl]` table to your front matter to select variants:

```toml
[tpl]
figure = "wide"
callout_note = "minimal"
```

This tells *Calepin* to look for `figure.wide.html` instead of `figure.html`, and `callout_note.minimal.html` instead of `callout_note.html`. If the variant file does not exist, the default template is used.

## File naming

Variant templates follow the pattern `{name}.{variant}.{ext}`:

```
templates/html/figure.html          # default
templates/html/figure.wide.html     # variant "wide"
templates/html/figure.compact.html  # variant "compact"
```

Resolution checks the target directory first, then the writer directory, then `common/`:

1. `{target}/{name}.{variant}.{ext}` (e.g., `website/figure.wide.html`)
2. `{writer}/{name}.{variant}.{ext}` (e.g., `html/figure.wide.html`)
3. `common/{name}.{variant}.jinja`

## Example: wide figures

Create `templates/html/figure.wide.html` in your sidecar:

```html
<figure id="{{cfg.id}}" style="max-width:none">
{{clp.content}}
{%- if cfg.caption %}<figcaption>{{cfg.caption}}</figcaption>{%- endif %}
</figure>
```

Then in any document that needs full-width figures:

```toml
[tpl]
figure = "wide"
```

All figures in that document use the wide variant. Other documents keep the default.

## Multiple variants

You can switch multiple templates at once:

```toml
[tpl]
figure = "wide"
code_source = "plain"
authors = "compact"
```

Each key is a template name, each value is the variant suffix.

## Scope

The `[tpl]` table is per-document (set in front matter). It can also be set in `config.toml` to apply to all documents in a project:

```toml
# config.toml
[tpl]
figure = "wide"
```

Per-document settings override project-level settings.
